title: POC Eval Artifacts & Decision Handoff — Vanguard Analytics

Redwood to deliver benchmark runbook, security docs, and pricing by 2026-12-12; customer to provide sample prompt set and baseline metrics.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-09
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Morgan Blake (Redwood AE), Navin Patel (Redwood SE), Lisa Chen (Vanguard Head of ML), Markus Rivera (Vanguard Infra), Priya Singh (Vanguard PM)

Auto-summary: Quick scoping to lock acceptance artifacts and the go/no-go guardrails for the POC.

00:00 Morgan Blake: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick roll call — that is Morgan from Redwood, Navin, and on the Vangu ard side Lisa, Markus, Priya, right? (laughs)
00:28 Lisa Chen: Yep, that's us. Thanks Morgan. We kicked this off because we need to finalize the acceptance gating and what you will deliver for the benchmark.
00:45 Navin Patel: Great. I sent a draft runbook earlier — today let's lock the thresholds: latency, cost, and quality. Also confirm the artifacts for the report.
01:12 Markus Rivera: Before we get deep, small infra constraint — our traffic profile for the POC is bursty during ingestion windows, average token lengths are around 160, but tail goes to 2k a handful of times. Also we are sensitive to sending data off-prem for some datasets.
01:48 Priya Singh: Timeline wise, product wants a go/no-go decision by 12/19 so we can plan the sprint. So the benchmark needs to finish, and we need a report a couple days before that.
02:20 Morgan Blake: Ok that helps. Proposal: two-week benchmark window starting as soon as we have sample prompts and your baseline CSV. We'll run Hosted first then Dedicated if you want to test reserved. For acceptance gates, we suggest p95 latency < 200ms for short-form (under 512 tokens) and < 500ms for long-form up to 2k; cost per 1M tokens < $12 in hosted-mode as a comparator — those are placeholders we can tweak.
03:05 Lisa Chen: The p95 200ms target feels tight for us, we've seen 250-300 on our current stack. How do you measure p95 — end-to-end or internal?
03:32 Navin Patel: Good question. We measure server-side token generation p95 measured at the Redwood collector — so it excludes client network time; we'll provide both server-side and end-to-end columns in the CSV.
03:58 Lisa Chen: Ok, send me definitions. Also on quality, we need a pass/fail for hallucination under 5% on red-team prompts and maintain F1 > 0.78 on entity extraction tasks.
04:27 Morgan Blake: Noted. So quality thresholds: hallucination rate < 5% on red-team, F1 >= 0.78 for extraction. We'll need your test set labels to run those checks.
05:02 Markus Rivera: Security: we need SOC2 Type II evidence, SAML SSO for console, and KMS integration before we go production. For POC, audit logs and at-rest encryption are must-haves.
05:32 Navin Patel: We have a security packet — Morgan will share it. For POC we can run in Hosted with strict retention and bring-your-own-key for some customers; for fully air-gapped we have the Private option but that needs procurement.
06:05 Lisa Chen: Can you clarify the difference between Redwood Dedicated and Private? Sometimes the names get swapped internally.
06:22 Morgan Blake: Sure — Dedicated is reserved GPU pools in our cloud with predictable throughput. Private is a VPC/on-prem deployment where the control plane is private to you.
06:45 Priya Singh: On reporting, we prefer a single CSV with these columns: prompt_id, prompt_length_tokens, model_variant, run_timestamp, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, end_to_end_latency_ms, tokens_generated, cost_estimate_usd, hallucination_flag, extraction_f1. Can Redwood produce that?
07:20 Navin Patel: Yes — we can output that exact schema. We'll also include a summary PDF with run notes and the raw model logs as gzipped JSON for debugging.
07:45 Lisa Chen: For datasets, we can provide a canonical 10k prompt set and a 1k red-team set. We'll need instructions for formatting.
08:12 Morgan Blake: We'll provide a template CSV and a script to upload. Navin, can you confirm the sample size for statistical significance?
08:30 Navin Patel: For p95 estimates we recommend at least 5k samples per model variant; 10k is ideal. For quality metrics like F1, depends on class balance — we'll run stratified sampling.
09:05 Markus Rivera: If we do multiple model variants, will costs balloon? Need to understand token and compute cost per run.
09:22 Morgan Blake: We'll include cost per 1k tokens and total compute hours in the report. We'll also attach a cost-normalized table to compare variants.
09:48 Priya Singh: About go/no-go: we need an explicit pass/fail rubric — if any threshold fails on critical metrics we fail, but define critical vs advisory.
10:05 Navin Patel: Proposal: Critical gates = p95 latency, hallucination rate, and F1 extraction. Advisory gates = cost and p50 latency. If any critical gate fails by more than 10% we'll mark go/no-go as fail and recommend remediation steps.
10:42 Lisa Chen: That makes sense. Can you quantify the 10%? Example: if p95 target is 200ms and we observe 220ms is that fail?
11:00 Navin Patel: 10% over target would be 220ms — yes that triggers a fail but we'll surface the distribution and config suggestions (batching, kv-cache, quantization).
11:28 Morgan Blake: We'll also include a regression delta relative to your baseline CSV. So acceptance isn't in a vacuum.
11:46 Lisa Chen: Good. For the reporting format, can you embed the run parameters: sequence length, temperature, top_p etc?
12:02 Navin Patel: Absolutely. Each row includes model params and the seed.
12:20 Priya Singh: Will you run deterministic runs or do multiple seeds?
12:30 Navin Patel: We'll run both: a deterministic set (seeded) for reproducibility and a stochastic set to measure variability.
12:50 Markus Rivera: Network egress — if we run Hosted, what IP ranges will you call from? Need for firewall whitelisting.
13:05 Morgan Blake: We'll provide an IP range list and temporary access tokens. Markus, you mentioned some data can't leave network — for those we could do a dedicated Private pilot but that's a procurement lift.
13:40 Lisa Chen: Ok. On timelines, can you confirm final deliverables?
13:50 Morgan Blake: Yes: runbook + CSV schema (by 12/12), Redwood to kickoff hosted runs once we receive prompt set (aim to begin 12/14), first results and raw CSV by 12/16, review meeting 12/18, final recommendation 12/19.
14:18 Priya Singh: Sounds good. One more — what about error/failure counts? Need to see graceful degradation and timeout rates.
14:32 Navin Patel: We'll add error counts per 1k requests, timeouts, and fallback occurrences.
14:48 Lisa Chen: For the quality metrics, we defined hallucination under 5% — how do you compute hallucination?
15:00 Navin Patel: We use a mixture: automated heuristics for nonsensical outputs + human verification for the red-team subset. We'll supply raw flags in the CSV so you can audit.
15:22 Morgan Blake: Any competitors we should be aware of? Lisa: you mentioned Anthropic in the RFP?
15:30 Lisa Chen: Yes, we have an internal eval with Anthropic. We'll compare results side-by-side.
15:42 Priya Singh: Also OpenAI for baseline.
16:00 Morgan Blake: Noted. Regarding acceptance reporting, would Vanguard prefer a single summarized dashboard or zipped artifacts for offline review?
16:12 Lisa Chen: Zipped artifacts plus a one-page executive summary PDF. Technical teams need raw CSVs.
16:28 Navin Patel: We'll provide both. Report package will include: executive PDF, CSVs per run, raw logs, and a remediation suggestions doc.
16:50 Markus Rivera: If some metrics are close, can we run a mitigation pass — e.g., enable kv-cache or reduce batch size?
17:05 Navin Patel: Yes, we can run a mitigation phase: if a critical gate fails, we'll run a tuning pass (1-2 days) for configuration changes, then re-run the benchmark subset. That will be part of the runbook and the decision flow.
17:36 Lisa Chen: Ok, what about measurement windows — do we clear caches between runs?
17:46 Navin Patel: We'll control for warm vs cold cache. We'll report both cold-start and steady-state numbers.
18:02 Priya Singh: For the acceptance rubric language, can you send a short go/no-go decision template we can sign off on?
18:12 Morgan Blake: Yes — Morgan: I'll send a one-page signoff template along with the runbook.
18:30 Lisa Chen: On deliverables, please include an example report so leadership sees format.
18:42 Navin Patel: We'll attach a synthetic example with dummy numbers so format is validated.
19:00 Markus Rivera: One technical note — our current infra uses autoscaling that spikes latency during scale-up. Can you simulate that?
19:12 Navin Patel: We can run synthetic bursts and measure tail latency under load. We'll include a burst profile in the run plan.
19:40 Morgan Blake: I'm going to recap the acceptance thresholds we agreed: p95 latency server-side < 200ms (short) / < 500ms (long), hallucination < 5%, extraction F1 >= 0.78; critical gates. Cost advisory threshold < $12 per 1M tokens. Do you want those exact numbers in the signoff?
20:10 Lisa Chen: Put them in the signoff. We'll review but those look fine as starting points.
20:28 Priya Singh: Ok. Anything else on reporting format?
20:35 Lisa Chen: Include provenance for each prompt (which dataset it came from) and a mapping file.
20:45 Navin Patel: Will do.
21:00 Morgan Blake: Next steps recap: we'll send the runbook + CSV schema and signoff template by Monday 12/12. You'll provide prompt set and baseline by 12/13. Navin will run smoke tests and deliver initial CSV by 12/16 and we'll meet 12/18 for go/no-go.
21:30 Lisa Chen: That timeline works.
22:00 Morgan Blake: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email and put the runbook in the shared folder.

End transcript notes: occasional transcription artifacts present (company names and some acronyms may be slightly off).
